newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Reebok estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Reebok estimates cut.

text.p: Two research firms cut their earnings estimates on Reebok International Ltd, but one firm raised its rating on the footwear firm's stock to accumulate from buy.
Analysts with Dean Witter and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette said they cut their earnings estimates after Reebok reported weaker third quarter earnings late Thursday.

But Dean Witter analyst Scott Emerman said he raised his rating on the stock to accumulate from neutral because many shareholders left the company as a result of its "Dutch auction" share tender in late August.

"I think a lot of potential holders got out. The people who are still in the stock are willing to give it some time," Emerman told Reuters. "I think that there's some protection on the downside there, and there could be some positive news."

Emerman said futures orders from U.S. specialty footwear stores, such as Foot Locker, appear strong and point towards renewed strength in the industry in the second half of the year, driving Reebok shares higher.
He cut his 1996 earnings estimate to $2.00 per share from $2.05 and his 1997 estimate to $2.55 from $2.70. Reebok reported earnings of $2.64 per share in 1995.

Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst Dana Eisman Cohen cut her earnings estimate for the fourth quarter to $0.44 per share from $0.52, for 1996 to $2.10 per share from $2.30 and for 1997 to $2.50 from $2.70, according to a research report.

Eisman Cohen wrote that although U.S. orders for the first quarter are up, "It is too early to signal a turnaround given competitive pressure from Nike Inc and Adidas AG, and the pressure on gross margins in 1997 due to the introduction of new models and brand building activities." She wrote that she continues to rate Reebok as "market performance."
